title: On the ubiquity of uniformly dominant local rings
summary: Let R be a d-dimensional Cohen-Macaulay complete local ring with infinite residue field k. The dominant index $\operatorname{dx}(R)$ is by definition the least number of extensions necessary to build k in the singularity category $\operatorname{D^{sg}}$ out of each nonzero object, up to finite direct sums, direct summands and shifts. The local ring R is called uniformly dominant if $\operatorname{dx}(R)$ is finite.
